full_judgment: 6. Defendant No. 1, the Mill and Defendant No. 2, proprietor of the Mill contested the suit by filing joint written statement admitting taking of loan but contending that there was no cause of action for filling the suit, that the suit was barred by limitation and by estoppel, weaver and acquiescence and that same had been filed with bad motive. The definite case of the defendants was that as per circular of the 3rd IDA credit defendant No. 2 submitted project profile to the plaintiff-bank, here in after in brief the Bank, in prescribed form for 3rd IDA credit and the Bank upon evaluating the project at Tk. 24,57,120/- (without taking into consideration the amount spent in building Mill Building, land development, installation of electricity etc) accepted the same, that the Bank sanctioned Tk. 9,70,000/- being Tk, 7,00,000/- cash finance and Tk. 2,70,000/- as working capital which were 35% of the project value and not 70% as required under the IDA Credit that instead of releasing money from IDA Credit the Bank saddled the*defendants on 01.09.1984 with cash credit scheme for Tk. 3,00,000/- initially which later on raised to Tk, 4,00,000/- the defendant No. 2 spent Tk. 10,00,000/- from his own fund for construction of the Mill-Building etc. in anticipation of reimbursement form loan since in the circular it was mentioned that the credit would be admissible to cover 70% of the cost of the project to be newly set up, that period of loan for capital finance was up to 12 years including grace period of 2 to 3 years maturity period for working capital was up to 5 years including grace period, that although in the IDA circular there was clear mention that 70% of the costs of new project under the credit would be paid but the Bank disbursed only Tk. 7,00,000/- as capital finance and Tk. 2,70,000/-as working capital totaling Tk. 9,70,000/-being 35% of the estimated project cost and that defendant No. 2 having had spent Tk. 10,00,000/- from his own capital he had to accept the loan advanced by the Bank under compulsion and that project having not fully financed by the Bank defendants faced scarcity of fund to run the mill in three shifts from one shift to make it more profitable and that in the said situation defendants requested the Bank to pray fresh loan- of Tk. 25,00,000/- and thereupon Bank having had asked for fresh security and the defendants having not been able to arrange fresh security since they had already mortgaged and hypothetical property worth more than Tk. 42,00,000/- to the Bank, but the Bank did not grant the Loan, that the amount advanced against cash credit limit of Tk. 3,00,000/- was illegally adjusted against the capital credit, that cash credit account balance while come to nil balance on 13th September, 1986 defendants requested for fresh loan against cash credit account but the plaintiff did not sanction the same that at a later period cash credit limit of Tk. 3,00,000/-was raised to Tk. 4,00,000/- on 1st February, 1987 and that out of the aforesaid amount of Tk, 4,00,000/- the Bank regularized their cash credit account and applied the same to the recovery of overdue amount Tk. 1,44,540/-fallen in arrear against the loan under IDA Credit etc. and that after such deduction form cash credit there remained only Tk. 25,000/-against the cash credit for running the Mill, that instead of advancing money for keeping the Mill running the Bank served legal notice for full payment of the loan including the loan made against IDA Credit and thereupon they had no option but to close down the Mill, which went into operation in August, 1984, in September, 1986. The defendant's contention is that the Bank had not right or legal authority to adjust IDA arrear installment' from C.0 Loan and that the defendants did not default in the payment of installments, rather they paid installment even after closing down the Mill and paid in total Tk. 5,08,620 on account of capital finance and working capital that defendant had to close the Mill by retrenching employees on paying their wages for which he incurred loss, that defendants paid Tk. 5,08,820/- upto December, 1987 as installment towards IDA cash credit loan, that the Bank has brought the suit prematurely only to take revenge against defendant. No. 2 who has already filed Money Suit No. 1 of 1990 against the Bank claiming compensations on different accounts and thus compelled the defendants to close down the Mill, It is also the contention of the defendants that the Bank grossly violated the terms and conditions of 3rd IDA credit circular by not giving loan to cover 70% of the cost of the project for which the defendants actually suffered from shortage of working capital for running the Mill viably, that the Bank instead of extending co-operation to the defendants brought the suit before the maturity of the IDA credit loan and that it is the Bank that compelled the defendants to close down the Mill in spite of their bonafide and good repayment schedule and that the plaintiff-Bank violated the terms of their own sanction letter and as such the suit brought by the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed.
